The department has top-ranked graduate and undergraduate programs and a strong research emphasis in machinery systems and postharvest process engineering. This position is part of a four-position cluster hire in AI in Agriculture across the College of Agriculture and Life Sciences to build research capacity in this area. Within this cluster, the Biological and Agricultural Engineering position focuses on AI-enabled autonomy, robotics, and precision operations in agricultural production. This position should address major challenges facing agriculture, such as efficiency, labor costs and availability, emerging biotic threats, water use and efficiency, and soil health. This position requires strong technical expertise in AI, sensing, automation and controls, or robotics, as well as knowledge of agricultural systems. Agriculture will be transformed in the coming decades by the adoption of robotics and data-driven systems. This position will lead innovation in development and in-field evaluation of these agricultural systems to increase farmer profitability, minimize resource use, and enhance the resilience of agriculture in Texas and beyond. While the candidate should have strong engineering expertise, transdisciplinary collaboration will be necessary for success in this role. Multiple resources are available through the college and university to support collaborative efforts. These include, but are not limited to, the Texas A&M Institute of Data Science and the High Performance Research Computing Center, which recently brought online the most powerful university supercomputer in the US. AgriLife has invested in data-driven agriculture initiatives such as the Automated Precision Phenotyping Greenhouse and the AgriTech Innovation Farm Hub. Furthermore, AgriLife has 13 research and extension centers across Texas and maintains strong connections with commodity groups and farmer organizations. The successful applicant will develop and teach courses in the Department of Biological and Agricultural Engineering. The individual will develop courses in agricultural autonomy/robotics for undergraduate and graduate students in Biological and Agricultural Engineering and Agricultural Systems Management. An undergraduate minor in AI-Enabled Agricultural Systems will be established with courses developed from this cluster hire. The individual will advise and mentor undergraduate and graduate students and other research personnel. The successful candidate will attract extramural funding and publish research in appropriate peer-reviewed journals. They will participate in service activities, both internally and professionally,

job_930ee08af6747ec5: About the Opportunity About the Woolston Lab The Woolston Lab at Northeastern University conducts research at the intersection of anaerobic microbiology, enzyme biochemistry, and natural products discovery. This position is funded by a National Institutes of Health (NIH) grant focused on unlocking the biosynthetic potential of Clostridial bacteria, a poorly understood but exceptionally rich source of novel bioactive compounds and unusual biosynthetic enzymes. The research program pursues two complementary directions. The first involves the biochemical and in vivo characterization of a newly discovered family of cobalamin-dependent radical S-adenosylmethionine (B12-rSAM) enzymes fused to non-ribosomal peptide synthetase (NRPS) adenylation domains. These enzymes are hypothesized to catalyze a stereoselective carbon backbone methylation reaction with no precedent in NRPS biochemistry. The second direction focuses on the discovery of novel antimicrobials from cellulolytic Clostridia through heterologous expression of biosynthetic gene clusters in a newly developed Clostridial chassis strain and activation of cryptic pathways in native producers via elicitor screening. Job Summary The Woolston Lab at Northeastern University seeks a Postdoctoral Research Associate to lead an exciting research program at the intersection of anaerobic microbiology, enzyme biochemistry, and natural products discovery. The Postdoctoral Research Associate will work closely with Prof. Woolston and a collaborative, interdisciplinary team of graduate students and undergraduate researchers. The Woolston Lab places a strong emphasis on open scientific exchange, mentorship, and a team-oriented culture in which postdoctoral researchers play a central role in shaping both the science and the intellectual environment of the group. The associate will be expected to conduct independent research, contribute to the mentorship of junior lab members, and communicate findings through publications, presentations, and reports to the funding agency. Minimum Qualifications Required PhD in microbiology, biochemistry, chemical engineering, or a related field. Demonstrated publication record of scientific findings in peer-reviewed journals. Experience investigating and characterizing natural products biosynthesis or experience purifying and functionally characterizing oxygen-sensitive enzymes (for example, iron-sulfur proteins and radical enzymes). Candidates with demonstrated expertise in both areas are especially competitive. Experience with modern bacterial genetics workflows, including cloning, genome editing, Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats (CRISPR)-based tools, and transposon mutagenesis. Experience with anaerobic microbiology techniques, including cultivation, handling, and experimental work under strictly anaerobic conditions. Bioinformatics skills relevant to genomics-driven natural products discovery, including genome mining, biosynthetic gene cluster analysis, sequence alignment, and annotation. Strong quantitative and statistical analysis skills for experimental data interpretation. Rigorous scientific documentation practices, including maintenance of detailed laboratory notebooks and research records. Excellent written and oral communication skills, with the ability to present research findings clearly to both specialist and general audiences. Demonstrated ability or strong potential to mentor undergraduate and graduate researchers. Ability to work independently and drive a research project forward while collaborating effectively within a team environment. The following outlines the professional responsibilities for outpatient cardiologists within the Department of Cardiovascular Medicine at the University of Texas Medical Branch (UTMB). These duties align with UTMB’s mission of excellence in patient care, education, research, and community engagement.
Clinical Care
· Conduct outpatient cardiology clinics for new, return, and follow-up patients.
· Order, interpret, and act upon diagnostic tests (e.g., ECG, echocardiography, stress testing, Holter monitoring, ).
· Develop and manage individualized care plans in collaboration with multidisciplinary teams.
· Coordinate referrals to subspecialty services (e.g., electrophysiology, interventional cardiology, heart failure).
· Manage medication regimens, including initiation, titration, and monitoring.
· Provide same-day patient access when clinically indicated.
· Respond to patient and referring provider inquiries in a timely manner.
Academic & Teaching Responsibilities
· Teach and mentor medical students, residents, and fellows during outpatient clinics.
· Participate in didactic teaching sessions, case conferences, and journal clubs for cardiology fellows and at medical school.
· Contribute to curriculum development for cardiovascular education.
· Supervise trainee documentation and ensure adherence to institutional standards.
Research & Scholarly Activity
· Participate in clinical research projects, including patient recruitment for trials.
· Publish scholarly articles, abstracts, or presentations in the field of cardiology.
· Support quality improvement projects focused on ambulatory cardiology care.
Administrative Duties
· Document patient encounters promptly and accurately in the electronic medical record (EMR).
· Attend departmental and divisional meetings.
· Collaborate with clinic management to optimize patient flow and access.
· Participate in institutional committees as assigned.
· Contribute to development of clinical protocols, pathways, and best practices.
Quality, Safety, & Compliance
· Monitor clinical outcomes and participate in performance improvement initiatives.
· Ensure compliance with institutional, state, and federal healthcare regulations.
· Maintain appropriate credentialing, licensure, and continuing medical education (CME) requirements.
· Participate in peer review and morbidity/mortality conferences.
Professional Development & Community Engagement
· Attend & participate in national and regional cardiology conferences.
· Engage in outreach to referring providers and community organizations.
· Represent the institution in professional societies and advocacy efforts.
Minimum Qualifications
MD degree or equivalent, Board certified or eligible in ABIM Cardiovascular Diseases. Must have completed an ACGME-accredited internal medicine residency. Possess or eligible for full medical license in the State of Texas.
